newsitem.title: INDIA: Four die in landslide after heavy rains in Bombay.
newsitem.headline: Four die in landslide after heavy rains in Bombay.

text.p: Four men were killed when their hut was razed by a landslide after heavy rain in a northwestern Bombay suburb early on Thursday, police and witnesses said.
"The four were taken to hospital, but were already dead," city police officials told Reuters. The incident occurred around 4 a.m. (2230 GMT on Wednesday), they added.
Witnesses said the men, all in their twenties, were migrant labourers living in a large slum in the suburb of Kandivli, 45 km (28 miles) from Bombay.
"Loose mud on the hill behind their hut came down in the rains, and just crushed it," said one witness. "None of the other huts in the row was affected."
Officials at the Bombay weather bureau said they expected heavy rain during the next 24 hours in the city, the adjoining Konkan coastal strip and the neighbouring resort state of Goa.
"Fishermen along the coast from Jaigad to Dahanu have been warned not to go to sea because of expected squally winds of 45 kmph to 55 kmph," one official said.
"Signal number three has been hoisted at all the ports, indicating that fishermen should not go fishing," he added.
